# CLAUDE.md -- chess-com-hide-material

**chess-com-hide-material** is a browser extension that hides the material balance (captured
pieces and the material advantage counter) on the Chess.com website, so the player has to keep
track of material on the board alone.

## Never leak secrets or sensitive information

Assume everything committed may become public, forever, history included. **Never write**, to any
file, commit message, issue, pull request, published page or external service:

- **Secrets:** passwords, tokens, API keys, Chess.com credentials, browser extension store
  (Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons) credentials or signing keys of any kind, even expired or
  fake-looking ones.
- **Identifying details beyond what the project already names:** IP addresses, MAC addresses,
  e-mail addresses, Chess.com usernames, share names, serial numbers, paths that reveal more than
  the repository root, and **machine names** and anything describing the developer's machines,
  how many there are, their hardware or age: a machine is named by its role alone, never by its
  hostname, in files and in conversation alike. Write as generally as the point allows.
- **Personal or household information:** schedules, habits, travel, where the developer works or
  lives.

Real values live only in gitignored local files, with committed examples holding placeholders.
Before writing a file the developer may commit, check it for any of the above; when in doubt,
leave it out and ask. A leak already committed cannot be fixed by a later commit: say so at once,
so the developer can rewrite history and rotate the secret.

**The same holds in conversation:** neither Claude nor the developer mentions any of the above in
a chat. Claude never brings it up, not even to quote what it found; it names the file and line
instead. When the developer's message or pasted output carries some (a prompt with the user name,
a path, a screenshot with a username), Claude says so in one line, without repeating it, so the
developer can be more careful next time.

## No autonomous writes allowed

The development of this project assumes that access to NotebookEdit, Bash,
and Monitor is fully denied to Claude. As a consequence, Git is also
fully denied.

## claude/ organization

Each repository has its own `claude/` directory (prose, distinct from the
`.claude/` harness config), holding `TODO.md` plus `active/`, `done/`, and
`archived/`.

- `active/`: work in progress.
- `done/`: completed, verified work, moved from `active/` as-is, no rename.
- `archived/`: superseded/abandoned/stale docs, moved here as-is with
  a "superseded, see X" note if applicable.

Source code must never reference a `claude/` document (bare filename or
path) -- inline the "why" directly in the code instead. Fix existing
violations opportunistically, not as a sweep.

Within `claude/`, docs may reference each other, but only by bare filename,
because filenames survive moves between the three subdirectories; paths do not.

## Design first, implement later

Do not rush off implementing. First discuss the design thoroughly, then write
the implementation plan as a document in `claude/active/`, and only then apply
it.

## Fenced blocks

When you want the developer to run something themselves, such as shell
commands or a commit, put it inside a fenced block so that they can copy it.
Put each command in its own fenced block: three consecutive commands are
three fenced blocks, never one block holding all three. Commit messages
must be one line only.

## Development platform: Windows

The extension is developed and tested on native Windows. The shell is **Git
Bash**, never PowerShell or cmd: every command in a fenced block uses Bash
syntax.

- Line endings are governed by `.gitattributes`: every text file is stored
  LF and checked out with the OS's native endings, CRLF on Windows, except
  `*.sh` which is always LF.
- Git Bash rewrites arguments that look like Unix paths when calling native
  Windows programs; prefix the command with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` when that
  bites.

## Chess.com is a moving target

Chess.com's markup is not a public API and changes without notice. Selectors
must target the most stable hooks available (semantic class names or data
attributes over generated or positional ones), and every selector the
extension depends on lives in one place, with a comment saying which page and
element it matches. The extension must fail safe: if a selector stops matching,
the page keeps working and nothing else is hidden by mistake.

The extension only hides content locally in the developer's browser. It never
sends requests of its own to Chess.com, never automates play, and never reads
or transmits game data elsewhere, in keeping with Chess.com's fair play rules.

## Licensing

The project is AGPLv3 only (`LICENSE`, `AGPL-3.0-only`): the developer's goal
is that nobody makes money by forking or using the code. GPLv3 code may be
combined with it (AGPLv3 section 13).

## No em dashes

Never write em dashes (—) or en dashes (–) to any file in this
repository, Markdown or otherwise. Write a double hyphen (--) instead.
Ordinary hyphens (-) are fine.
